content: A company like Southern Africa Mining Supplies (Pty) Ltd would build its entire strategic identity around its strong local content and B-BBEE credentials. Their global ownership structures make it difficult to score well on the ownership element of B-BBEE. They invest heavily in skills development programs, enterprise and supplier development (ESD) initiatives, and corporate social investment (CSI) to improve their B-BBEE scorecards. They might form joint ventures with local, black-owned partners or create 'empowerment' distribution channels. The company cannot view local content and B-BBEE as a mere administrative burden; it must be integrated into the core of its business strategy. They want suppliers who are proactive, innovative, and aligned with their strategic goals, such as safety, environmental sustainability, and digital transformation. For Alpha Industries, this means a shift in approach. This means that a competitor like SAMS , with its Level 1 B-BBEE certificate, has an inherent and significant advantage. This involves submitting a vast amount of company information, including financial statements, B-BBEE certificates, safety statistics, and quality certifications.
